blocks.text: User roles control access to features and actions within the Agentic Security Operations Platform (Agentic SecOps Platform). After creating users in your account, you can assign roles to define their access and permissions. You can choose from predefined system roles, or the account admin can create and assign custom roles. Custom roles are configured to reflect your internal policies or workflows.
When new Agentic SecOps Platform features are released, related permissions must be manually added to your custom roles.

blocks.item: In the Agentic SecOps Platform Admin Portal, click the Profile menu in the top navigation bar, and click Account Settings.
See image.
In the left-side navigation, go to Permissions > Roles.
See image.
On the Roles page, you can create a custom role in the following ways:
Click Create.
See image.
Duplicate an existing role. Hover over the role in the table and click the Duplicate Role icon (), or select the role and click Duplicate at the top of the page.
See image.
The duplicated role is added to the list of roles.
You can't duplicate the system Admin role.
On the New Role page:
Role Name: Enter a name for the role.
Resource: Select the relevant permissions (e.g., Read, Create, Edit, Delete, Audit) for each resource.

To apply the same permission to all items in a category, select the checkbox at the top of the category. Selecting a higher-level permission (e.g., Edit) automatically enables required lower-level permissions (e.g., Read).
See image.
Click Next.
The Add Users window appears.
Select the users you want to assign to the role, and click Add.
See image.
The users assigned to the role are listed in the table.
To add more users, click Add Users.
To remove users:
Hover over a user, and click the Remove From List icon.
Select the checkboxes next to one or more users, and click Remove From Role.
See image.
Click Finish.
The selected users' roles are updated immediately.

blocks.text: Role permissions are organized into distinct categories, each representing a group of related system resources. Within each category, you can select permissions (i.e., Read, Create, Edit, Delete, and Audit) for custom roles to control access and operations on those resources. These assignments form a permissions matrix for the custom roles that are subsequently assigned to users.
